title: Remote Work Policy Handbook
text:
Purpose. This handbook explains when employees may work away from the main office, how managers approve those arrangements, and which costs the company covers. It applies to every department and every contract type, including part-time staff.

Eligibility. Most roles that need a computer and a phone line qualify for some remote time. Employees approved for remote work may work remotely up to three days per week, and any additional days require written director sign-off. New hires wait ninety days before submitting a request so that onboarding happens in person. Roles that handle physical inventory, reception duty, or classified material are exempt from this policy entirely.

Approval process. Submit the standard request form at least two weeks before the first remote day. Your manager checks coverage for the front desk, schedules at least one overlap hour with the team, and confirms your home connection meets the security baseline. Managers answer every request within five business days, and declined requests come back with a written reason. Approvals renew each January, and either side can end an arrangement with two weeks of notice.

Equipment and expenses. The company loans a laptop, a monitor, and a headset, and IT ships them to your home. Employees provide their own desk, chair, and internet service. The company reimburses one ergonomic chair per employee every three years with a receipt. Travel to the office on remote days is not reimbursed.

Questions about this policy go to the people operations desk, not to individual managers. The handbook is reviewed every October and updated versions are announced in the all-hands meeting.
reference: Approved employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval, and requests must be submitted two weeks ahead.
